IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: House Committee on Early Learning & Children's Services (originally sponsored by Representatives Hinkle and Walsh)

Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring the petitioner in a child welfare case to provide the court with relevant documentation.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to documentation in child welfare proceedings;adding a new section to chapter 13.34 RCW; and creating new sections.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Several tragic child fatalities in the stateover the past years have highlighted the need to look closely atplacement decisions for children in the care of the state. The courtsplay a vital role in the placement decision making. In order to allowcourts to make the best decision for children, the courts must beprovided with accurate information. In several of the reviews conducted following child fatalityidentified situations, the caseworker provided summaries of relevantmaterial, rather than the documents themselves. These summaries wererelied upon and were later found to be inaccurate. The legislature finds that in order to facilitate the court actingin an oversight capacity, the caseworker must provide the court withdocumentation supporting assertions or recommendations made by thecaseworker.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 13.34 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In any proceeding under this chapter, if the department submits areport to the court in which the department is recommending a child beplaced with a parent after the child was removed from the parent due toabuse or neglect allegations, the department shall include thedocuments listed in subsections (1) through (4) of this section to thereport. The department shall include only these relevant documents andshall not attach the entire history of the parent or child. (1) If the report contains a recommendation, opinion, or assertionby the department relating to the parent's substance abuse treatment,mental health treatment, anger management classes, or domestic violenceclasses, the department shall attach the document upon which therecommendation, opinion, or assertion was based. The documentation mayinclude the progress report or evaluation submitted by the provider,but may not include the entire history with the provider. (2) If the report contains a recommendation, opinion, or assertionby the department relating to the parent's visitation with the child,the department shall attach the document upon which the recommendation,opinion, or assertion was based. The documentation may include themost recent visitation report, a visitation report referencing aspecific incident alleged in the report, or summary of the visitationprepared by the person who supervised the visitation. Thedocumentation attached to the report shall not include the entirevisitation history. (3) If the report contains a recommendation, opinion, or assertionby the department relating to the psychological status of the parent,the department shall attach the document upon which the recommendation,opinion, or assertion was based. The documentation may include theprogress report, evaluation, or summary submitted by the provider, butshall not include the entire history of the parent. (4) If the report contains a recommendation, opinion, or assertionby the department relating to injuries to the child that occurred whilein the care of the parent, the department shall attach a summary of thephysician's report relating to the recommendation, opinion, orassertion by the department.
This act shall be known and cited as theRaphael Gomez act.
